boundaryClasses.claim: Moving the window's lower bound 479000 ms later leaves the same header times accepted: only the upper bound decides, which is what makes this an anchor rather than interval membership.
The inclusive upper bound of the longest short validity range opening at 1700000000000 — the largest end_time any such commit can carry.
One millisecond above the bound is already rejected; the accepted set is a single point, not a range.

dueEventClasses.claim: A deposit includable one millisecond after the maximum accepted end_time is not due under that end_time, would be due under the far-future end_time, and the far-future end_time is exactly what the commit anchor refuses.
Taken a full year past the commit window to show the gap the anchor closes is unbounded, not an off-by-one.
Both halves of forced due-ness flip together under a far-future end_time, and both are held shut by the anchor.
